description: Review the security architecture of a system by mapping trust boundaries, authentication paths, data flow protections, network segmentation, and forensic logging readiness.

steps.description: Document all system components and map trust boundaries between them.

inputs.name: system-description
inputs.desc: Description of the system under review

inputs.name: architecture-diagrams
inputs.desc: Available architecture diagrams or topology docs

outputs.name: component-inventory
outputs.desc: Cataloged list of all system components

outputs.name: trust-boundary-map
outputs.desc: Map showing trust boundaries between components

process: Enumerate all system components including services, databases, message queues, and external integrations
Identify trust boundaries at network, process, and data layers
Map data flows that cross each trust boundary
Document assumptions about trust at each boundary

steps.description: Evaluate the authentication and authorization architecture for design weaknesses.

inputs.name: trust-boundary-map
inputs.desc: Trust boundary map from prior step

outputs.name: authn-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of authentication mechanisms across all entry points

outputs.name: authz-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of authorization model and enforcement points

process: Catalog all authentication mechanisms in use (passwords, tokens, certificates, MFA)
Trace the authorization model from request to resource access
Check for consistent enforcement at every trust boundary crossing
Identify any paths that bypass authentication or authorization checks

steps.description: Assess data flow protections including encryption in transit and at rest, and data integrity controls.

outputs.name: encryption-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of encryption coverage for data in transit and at rest

outputs.name: integrity-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of data integrity controls across flows

process: Map every data flow path and classify by sensitivity
Verify encryption protocols and cipher suites for data in transit
Check encryption at rest for each storage system
Assess integrity controls (signatures, checksums, HMAC) on critical data paths

steps.description: Review network architecture and segmentation for lateral movement risks.

outputs.name: segmentation-findings
outputs.desc: Findings on network segmentation effectiveness

outputs.name: lateral-movement-risks
outputs.desc: Identified lateral movement paths between segments

process: Map network zones and verify segmentation enforcement (firewalls, VLANs, security groups)
Test for overly permissive rules that allow unnecessary cross-zone traffic
Identify lateral movement paths an attacker could exploit from each zone
Check for flat network segments where segmentation should exist

steps.description: Check that resilience and failover mechanisms do not weaken security posture.

outputs.name: resilience-security-findings
outputs.desc: Security issues in resilience and failover paths

outputs.name: failover-exposure-map
outputs.desc: Map of security controls that degrade during failover

process: Identify all failover and redundancy mechanisms
Check whether failover paths bypass security controls present in normal operation
Verify that backup systems maintain the same security configuration as primary
Test that degraded-mode operation does not expose new attack surfaces

steps.description: Assess whether logging architecture supports forensic investigation after a breach.

inputs.name: authn-assessment
inputs.desc: Authentication assessment for correlating log gaps with auth events

outputs.name: logging-coverage-map
outputs.desc: Map of which events are logged across the system

outputs.name: forensic-readiness-score
outputs.desc: Score indicating how well logs support incident investigation

process: Inventory all log sources and what events they capture
Check log integrity protections (tamper-evident, write-once, centralized collection)
Verify retention periods meet investigation timelines
Test that security-relevant events (authentication, authorization, data access) are captured with enough detail for reconstruction

steps.description: Compile all findings into the security architecture review report with risk ratings and recommendations.

outputs.name: security-architecture-report
outputs.desc: Complete security architecture review report

outputs.name: prioritized-remediation-list
outputs.desc: Ranked list of remediation actions by risk severity

process: Consolidate findings from all assessment areas
Rate each finding by severity (critical, high, medium, low) using likelihood and impact
Write remediation recommendations for each finding
Produce the final report with executive summary, detailed findings, and prioritized action plan

description: Run a collaborative purple team exercise where red team executes MITRE ATT&CK techniques while blue team measures detection, then tune detections for gaps found.

steps.description: Define attack scenarios and select MITRE ATT&CK techniques to test.

inputs.name: threat-model
inputs.desc: Threat model or threat intelligence for the target environment

inputs.name: environment-scope
inputs.desc: Description of the environment to test

outputs.name: attack-plan
outputs.desc: Ordered list of ATT&CK techniques to execute

outputs.name: success-criteria
outputs.desc: Criteria for each technique defining what counts as successful execution

process: Review the threat model to identify relevant threat actors and their TTPs
Select ATT&CK techniques aligned with those TTPs across the kill chain
Order techniques into logical attack paths from initial access through impact
Define success criteria and observable indicators for each technique

steps.description: Execute each ATT&CK technique while blue team observes in real time.

inputs.name: attack-plan
inputs.desc: Ordered list of techniques to execute

outputs.name: execution-log
outputs.desc: Log of each technique execution with timestamps, tools used, and outcome

outputs.name: blue-team-observations
outputs.desc: Blue team notes on what they observed for each technique

process: Execute each technique in the planned order using approved tools
Record the exact commands, tools, and timestamps for each execution
Blue team independently logs what alerts or indicators they observed
Pause between techniques to allow blue team to finish documentation

steps.description: Measure detection coverage by comparing red team executions against blue team observations.

outputs.name: detection-scorecard
outputs.desc: Matrix of techniques tested vs detection status (detected, partial, missed)

outputs.name: coverage-percentage
outputs.desc: Overall detection coverage percentage

process: Align each executed technique with corresponding blue team observations
Score each technique as detected (alert fired and investigated), partial (alert fired but not triaged), or missed
Calculate overall detection coverage as a percentage of techniques tested
Identify patterns in misses (particular tactics, data sources, or detection logic gaps)

steps.description: Analyze missed and partially detected techniques to identify the root cause of each gap.

inputs.name: detection-scorecard
inputs.desc: Scorecard of detection outcomes per technique

outputs.name: gap-analysis
outputs.desc: Root cause analysis for each detection gap

outputs.name: missing-data-sources
outputs.desc: Data sources needed but not currently ingested

process: For each missed technique, determine whether the gap is missing data source, missing rule, or rule misconfiguration
For partial detections, determine why the alert was not investigated (noise, low priority, unclear)
Catalog all missing data sources that would close gaps
Rank gaps by risk, considering the technique's position in the kill chain

steps.description: Tune existing detection rules and create new rules to close identified gaps.

inputs.name: gap-analysis
inputs.desc: Root cause analysis of detection gaps

inputs.name: missing-data-sources
inputs.desc: Data sources needed to close gaps

outputs.name: tuned-rules
outputs.desc: List of rules tuned with before and after configurations

outputs.name: new-rules
outputs.desc: New detection rules created to cover previously missed techniques

process: Tune existing rules that produced false negatives by adjusting thresholds or logic
Write new detection rules for techniques where no rule existed
Prioritize rule creation by kill chain position (prefer early detection)
Document each rule change with rationale

steps.description: Re-execute previously missed techniques to validate that new and tuned rules detect them.

inputs.name: execution-log
inputs.desc: Original execution log for replay reference

outputs.name: validation-results
outputs.desc: Results of re-testing previously missed techniques

outputs.name: remaining-gaps
outputs.desc: Any techniques that still evade detection after tuning

process: Re-execute each previously missed technique using the same tools and methods
Verify that new or tuned rules fire alerts correctly
Record any remaining gaps that need further work (additional data sources, custom detections)
Confirm no new false positives were introduced by the tuning

steps.description: Compile the purple team exercise report with coverage metrics, gap analysis, and improvement outcomes.

outputs.name: purple-team-report
outputs.desc: Full purple team exercise report

outputs.name: detection-improvement-delta
outputs.desc: Before and after detection coverage comparison

process: Summarize the exercise scope, techniques tested, and methodology
Present the before and after detection coverage percentages
Document each gap found, its root cause, and the fix applied
List remaining gaps with a remediation timeline and owner

description: Set up a bug bounty program from scope definition through platform selection, triage workflow, and policy publication.

steps.description: Define the program scope and rules of engagement for bug bounty hunters.

inputs.name: asset-inventory
inputs.desc: Inventory of assets (domains, APIs, mobile apps) to include

inputs.name: risk-tolerance
inputs.desc: Organization risk tolerance and testing constraints

outputs.name: program-scope
outputs.desc: Defined in-scope and out-of-scope assets and test types

outputs.name: rules-of-engagement
outputs.desc: Rules researchers must follow during testing

process: Classify each asset by criticality and readiness for external testing
Define in-scope targets (URLs, IP ranges, mobile apps) and explicitly list out-of-scope items
Write rules of engagement covering prohibited actions (DoS, social engineering, data exfiltration)
Define safe harbor language protecting researchers who follow the rules

steps.description: Design severity classifications and corresponding reward tiers.

outputs.name: severity-tiers
outputs.desc: Severity classification scheme with examples

outputs.name: reward-schedule
outputs.desc: Payment amounts for each severity level and asset type

process: Define severity levels (critical, high, medium, low, informational) with concrete examples
Set reward amounts for each severity level, scaled by asset criticality
Define bonus criteria (first report of a class, chain of bugs, exceptional write-up)
Document what does and does not qualify for a reward (duplicates, known issues, scanner output)

steps.description: Evaluate and select the bug bounty platform (managed service or self-hosted).

outputs.name: platform-selection
outputs.desc: Selected platform with rationale

outputs.name: platform-configuration
outputs.desc: Configuration requirements for the chosen platform

process: Compare managed platforms (HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Intigriti) against self-hosted options
Evaluate by researcher pool size, triage support, cost structure, and integration capabilities
Select the platform that fits budget and maturity level
Document the configuration needed (SSO, ticketing integration, payment processing)

steps.description: Build the internal security response process for handling incoming reports.

outputs.name: response-sla-matrix
outputs.desc: SLA targets for triage, validation, fix, and payment by severity

outputs.name: escalation-procedures
outputs.desc: Escalation paths for critical findings and disputes

process: Define SLA targets: time to first response, time to triage, time to fix, time to payment
Assign roles: who triages, who validates, who approves payment, who communicates with researchers
Build escalation procedures for critical severity and for researcher disputes
Create templates for common responses (duplicate, out of scope, accepted, needs info)

steps.description: Design the submission intake and triage workflow from report to resolution.

outputs.name: triage-workflow
outputs.desc: Step-by-step triage workflow with decision points

outputs.name: ticketing-integration-spec
outputs.desc: Specification for integrating with internal ticketing systems

process: Map the workflow from report submission through triage, validation, fix, retest, and payment
Define decision points: is it a duplicate, is it in scope, can it be reproduced, what severity
Specify the ticketing integration so validated reports create internal bugs automatically
Build the feedback loop where researchers are notified at each state change

steps.description: Write the public-facing program policy page and launch the program.

inputs.name: program-scope
inputs.desc: Program scope and rules of engagement

inputs.name: triage-workflow
inputs.desc: Triage workflow for reference in policy

outputs.name: policy-page-content
outputs.desc: Complete policy page text ready to publish

outputs.name: launch-checklist
outputs.desc: Checklist of items to verify before going live

process: Write the policy page with scope, rules, rewards, safe harbor, and SLA commitments
Review for legal accuracy (safe harbor, exclusions, payment terms)
Build the launch checklist: internal team ready, platform configured, payment method set up, legal approved
Plan the launch announcement (private invite first, then public)

description: Assess and tune SIEM detection effectiveness by inventorying log sources, testing coverage against ATT&CK, and creating or adjusting correlation rules.

steps.description: Inventory all log sources feeding the SIEM and profile their ingestion rates and reliability.

inputs.name: siem-configuration
inputs.desc: Current SIEM configuration and data source list

inputs.name: environment-topology
inputs.desc: Network and system topology of the monitored environment

outputs.name: log-source-inventory
outputs.desc: Complete inventory of log sources with ingestion rates and gaps

outputs.name: coverage-gaps
outputs.desc: Systems or services not sending logs to the SIEM

process: Extract the list of all configured log sources from the SIEM
Compare against the environment topology to find systems not sending logs
Measure ingestion rate, latency, and parse failure rate for each source
Flag any sources with intermittent delivery or high error rates

steps.description: Test each correlation rule for detection accuracy and false positive rate.

outputs.name: rule-effectiveness-matrix
outputs.desc: Matrix showing each rule, its trigger rate, true positive rate, and false positive rate

outputs.name: noisy-rules
outputs.desc: Rules with unacceptable false positive rates

process: Catalog all active correlation rules and their trigger counts over the past 30 days
Sample triggered alerts and classify as true positive, false positive, or undetermined
Calculate the true positive and false positive rates for each rule
Identify rules that fire frequently but rarely produce actionable alerts

steps.description: Map detection rules to MITRE ATT&CK techniques and identify uncovered techniques.

outputs.name: attack-coverage-heatmap
outputs.desc: Heatmap showing which ATT&CK techniques are covered by rules and data

outputs.name: uncovered-techniques
outputs.desc: List of ATT&CK techniques with no detection rule or insufficient data

process: Tag each correlation rule with the ATT&CK technique(s) it detects
Build the coverage heatmap across all tactics and techniques
Identify techniques with no rule and techniques with rules but missing data sources
Prioritize uncovered techniques by relevance to the organization's threat model

steps.description: Tune high-noise rules to reduce false positives without losing true positive detection.

outputs.name: tuned-rule-configs
outputs.desc: Updated rule configurations with changes documented

outputs.name: expected-noise-reduction
outputs.desc: Projected false positive reduction per tuned rule

process: For each noisy rule, analyze the false positive triggers to find common patterns
Adjust thresholds, add exclusions, or refine conditions to filter out false positives
Validate that the tuned rule still detects the original true positive scenarios
Document each change with before and after expected alert volumes

steps.description: Create new correlation rules for previously uncovered ATT&CK techniques.

inputs.name: log-source-inventory
inputs.desc: Available data sources for rule logic

outputs.name: new-rule-definitions
outputs.desc: New rule definitions ready for deployment

outputs.name: data-source-requests
outputs.desc: Requests for new data sources needed by rules that cannot be written with current data

process: For each prioritized technique, determine which data sources provide visibility
Write the detection logic using available log fields
Set initial thresholds conservatively to avoid alert fatigue
Flag techniques where detection requires a data source not yet ingested

steps.description: Assemble the SIEM tuning assessment report with before and after coverage metrics.

outputs.name: siem-tuning-report
outputs.desc: Complete SIEM tuning assessment report

outputs.name: coverage-improvement-summary
outputs.desc: Summary of coverage improvement before and after tuning

process: Compile all findings: log source gaps, noisy rules, coverage gaps, new rules
Calculate the coverage improvement: techniques covered before vs after
Estimate the noise reduction: projected alert volume before vs after tuning
Produce the report with executive summary, detailed findings, and implementation timeline

description: Audit the security of a microservices architecture by testing service-to-service authentication, authorization, API gateway controls, and distributed tracing data exposure.

steps.description: Map all microservices and their communication patterns.

inputs.name: service-registry
inputs.desc: Service registry or discovery system configuration

inputs.name: network-policies
inputs.desc: Network policies and firewall rules between services

outputs.name: service-topology
outputs.desc: Map of all services and their dependencies

outputs.name: communication-matrix
outputs.desc: Matrix showing which service calls which, over what protocol

process: Query the service registry for all registered services and their endpoints
Trace actual communication patterns from network logs or service mesh telemetry
Identify services communicating outside the expected patterns
Document protocols in use (gRPC, HTTP, AMQP, raw TCP) for each service pair

steps.description: Test service-to-service authentication for mTLS, JWT, and API key implementations.

outputs.name: authn-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of authentication tests for each service pair

outputs.name: unauthenticated-paths
outputs.desc: Service paths that accept unauthenticated requests

process: For each service pair, test whether requests without valid credentials are rejected
Verify mTLS certificate validation (expired, wrong CA, self-signed)
Test JWT validation (expired, wrong issuer, tampered signature, algorithm confusion)
Identify services that accept requests from any caller without authentication

steps.description: Test authorization boundaries to find broken access control between services.

outputs.name: authz-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of authorization boundary tests

outputs.name: privilege-escalation-paths
outputs.desc: Paths where one service can access another's resources beyond its intended scope

process: For each authenticated service pair, test access to resources outside the caller's intended scope
Check for horizontal privilege escalation (Service A accessing Service B's data for a different tenant)
Check for vertical privilege escalation (low-privilege service accessing admin endpoints)
Test whether internal services enforce authorization or rely solely on the API gateway

steps.description: Test the API gateway for bypass vulnerabilities and misconfigured security controls.

outputs.name: gateway-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of API gateway security tests

outputs.name: bypass-vulnerabilities
outputs.desc: Methods to bypass the gateway and reach services directly

process: Test for direct access to backend services bypassing the gateway (IP direct, alternate ports)
Test rate limiting effectiveness and bypass techniques
Check input validation at the gateway (oversized requests, malformed headers, path traversal)
Verify that the gateway enforces authentication before routing

steps.description: Test for abuse potential in circuit breaker and retry mechanisms.

outputs.name: retry-abuse-findings
outputs.desc: Findings on retry storm and circuit breaker abuse potential

outputs.name: cascading-failure-risks
outputs.desc: Paths where retry abuse could cause cascading failures

process: Test whether an attacker can trigger retry storms by causing specific error responses
Check whether circuit breakers can be manipulated to deny service to legitimate callers
Identify cascading failure paths where one service's failure causes unbounded retries in others
Verify that retry budgets and circuit breaker thresholds prevent amplification

steps.description: Audit distributed tracing for sensitive data exposure in trace spans and logs.

outputs.name: tracing-data-findings
outputs.desc: Sensitive data found in trace spans, tags, and logs

outputs.name: microservices-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete microservices security audit report

process: Sample trace data and inspect spans for PII, credentials, tokens, or internal identifiers
Check whether trace data is accessible to unauthorized parties
Verify that sensitive fields are redacted before traces are stored or exported
Compile all findings from all steps into the final microservices security audit report

description: Assess physical security of a facility by testing perimeter, access controls, surveillance, server room protections, and visitor management.

steps.description: Survey the facility perimeter and all entry points for physical weaknesses.

inputs.name: facility-description
inputs.desc: Description and floor plans of the facility

outputs.name: entry-point-inventory
outputs.desc: Inventory of all entry points with their access control type

outputs.name: perimeter-weaknesses
outputs.desc: Physical weaknesses found in the perimeter

process: Walk the full perimeter and document every entry point (doors, loading docks, windows, roof access)
Classify each entry point by access control type (badge, key, biometric, unlocked)
Identify weak points: propped doors, damaged locks, blind spots, accessible windows
Photograph and document each finding with location

steps.description: Test badge, biometric, and mantrap access control systems for bypass vulnerabilities.

inputs.name: entry-point-inventory
inputs.desc: Inventory of entry points and their controls

outputs.name: access-control-findings
outputs.desc: Findings from testing each access control system

outputs.name: bypass-methods
outputs.desc: Methods that successfully bypassed access controls

process: Test badge readers for cloning vulnerability, relay attacks, and expired badge acceptance
Test biometric systems for spoofing (silicone fingerprints, printed photos, replay)
Test mantraps for tailgating detection and anti-passback enforcement
Attempt to use social engineering to gain entry through controlled doors

steps.description: Test for tailgating and piggybacking vulnerabilities at controlled entry points.

outputs.name: tailgating-results
outputs.desc: Results of tailgating attempts at each entry point

outputs.name: employee-awareness-score
outputs.desc: Score indicating how often employees challenge or report tailgaters

process: Attempt to tailgate through each controlled entry point during various times of day
Record whether employees challenge the tailgater, hold the door, or ignore
Test during high-traffic periods (morning, lunch, shift change) vs low-traffic
Calculate the success rate and employee awareness score

steps.description: Assess surveillance camera coverage, monitoring, and recording integrity.

inputs.name: entry-point-inventory
inputs.desc: Entry point locations to verify camera coverage

outputs.name: camera-coverage-map
outputs.desc: Map showing camera locations, angles, and blind spots

outputs.name: monitoring-effectiveness
outputs.desc: Assessment of whether cameras are actively monitored and recordings are protected

process: Map all camera locations and their fields of view
Identify blind spots: areas without camera coverage, especially around entry points and sensitive areas
Verify that recordings are stored with integrity protections and adequate retention
Test whether the security operations center actively monitors feeds or only reviews after incidents

steps.description: Test access to server rooms, wiring closets, and other sensitive areas.

inputs.name: facility-description
inputs.desc: Facility layout with sensitive areas marked

inputs.name: bypass-methods
inputs.desc: Methods that worked at perimeter for potential reuse

outputs.name: sensitive-area-findings
outputs.desc: Findings from testing access to sensitive areas

outputs.name: physical-data-exposure
outputs.desc: Data exposure risks from physical access to equipment

process: Attempt to access server rooms, network closets, and executive areas using bypass methods
Check whether sensitive areas have additional controls beyond perimeter badges
Assess what data or systems could be compromised with physical access to each area
Check for unlocked network ports, exposed consoles, and visible credentials in sensitive areas

steps.description: Review visitor management procedures for security gaps.

inputs.name: tailgating-results
inputs.desc: Tailgating results to correlate with visitor controls

outputs.name: visitor-management-findings
outputs.desc: Findings from visitor management review

outputs.name: physical-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete physical security assessment report

process: Review the visitor registration and badge issuance process
Test whether visitor badges grant access beyond intended areas
Check whether visitors are escorted as required by policy
Compile all findings into the physical security assessment report with risk ratings and remediation

description: Test backup and disaster recovery security by verifying encryption, restoration, recovery objectives, ransomware resilience, and offsite integrity.

steps.description: Inventory all backup systems, schedules, and retention policies.

inputs.name: infrastructure-inventory
inputs.desc: Inventory of systems that need backup coverage

outputs.name: backup-inventory
outputs.desc: Complete inventory of backup systems with schedules and retention

outputs.name: unprotected-systems
outputs.desc: Systems or data sets not covered by any backup schedule

process: Catalog every backup system in operation (agent-based, snapshot, replication, tape)
Map each production system to its backup coverage and verify schedule adherence
Identify systems or datasets with no backup coverage
Verify that retention periods meet regulatory and business requirements

steps.description: Verify that backups are encrypted at rest and in transit.

outputs.name: encryption-verification-results
outputs.desc: Results of encryption verification for each backup system

outputs.name: key-management-findings
outputs.desc: Findings on backup encryption key management practices

process: Verify encryption in transit for each backup data flow
Verify encryption at rest for each backup storage location
Check key management: where keys are stored, who has access, rotation schedule
Test that backups cannot be read without the correct decryption key

steps.description: Test restoration from backup (full and incremental) to verify recoverability.

inputs.name: encryption-verification-results
inputs.desc: Encryption status for planning test decryption

outputs.name: restoration-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of each restoration test including time and completeness

outputs.name: data-integrity-verification
outputs.desc: Verification that restored data matches the original

process: Select a representative sample of backup sets across systems and types
Restore each to an isolated environment and measure the time required
Verify data integrity by comparing checksums or record counts against the source
Test both full and incremental restoration paths

steps.description: Measure actual recovery time and recovery point against documented objectives.

outputs.name: rto-rpo-comparison
outputs.desc: Comparison of actual recovery metrics against targets

outputs.name: objective-gaps
outputs.desc: Systems where actual recovery exceeds stated RTO or RPO

process: Calculate actual RTO from the restoration tests (time from failure to operational)
Calculate actual RPO from backup timestamps (data loss window)
Compare each system's actual metrics against its documented RTO and RPO targets
Flag systems where actual recovery exceeds targets by any amount

steps.description: Test whether backups are resilient to ransomware by checking for tampering and immutability.

inputs.name: key-management-findings
inputs.desc: Key management findings for attack path analysis

outputs.name: ransomware-resilience-results
outputs.desc: Results of ransomware resilience testing

outputs.name: immutability-status
outputs.desc: Whether each backup system enforces immutable storage

process: Test whether an attacker with admin access to production can also delete or modify backups
Check for immutable storage (WORM, object lock) on backup targets
Verify that backup credentials are not accessible from production systems
Test whether backup agents can be disabled or reconfigured by a compromised admin account

steps.description: Verify the integrity and accessibility of offsite or air-gapped backup copies.

outputs.name: offsite-integrity-results
outputs.desc: Verification results for offsite backup copies

outputs.name: backup-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete backup and recovery security report

process: Verify that offsite copies exist and are current
Test restoration from the offsite copy independently of primary backups
Confirm network isolation: offsite copies cannot be reached from production networks
Compile all findings into the backup and recovery security report with risk ratings

description: Review OAuth2 and OIDC implementation security by testing flows, redirect URIs, token management, scope escalation, PKCE, and token leakage vectors.

steps.description: Map all OAuth2 and OIDC flows in use across the application.

inputs.name: application-architecture
inputs.desc: Architecture of the application under review

outputs.name: flow-inventory
outputs.desc: Inventory of all OAuth flows with client types and grant types

outputs.name: client-classification
outputs.desc: Classification of each client as public or confidential

process: Identify all OAuth clients registered with the authorization server
Map each client to its grant type (authorization code, client credentials, device, implicit, ROPC)
Classify each client as public (SPA, mobile, CLI) or confidential (server-side)
Flag any use of deprecated flows (implicit, ROPC) that should be migrated

steps.description: Test for redirect URI manipulation and open redirect vulnerabilities.

inputs.name: oauth-configuration
inputs.desc: OAuth configuration with registered redirect URIs

outputs.name: redirect-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of redirect URI manipulation tests

outputs.name: open-redirect-findings
outputs.desc: Any open redirect vulnerabilities found

process: Test exact match enforcement: try adding path segments, query parameters, or fragments
Test for subdomain takeover of registered redirect domains
Test for open redirectors on the redirect URI domain that could be chained
Verify that wildcard or partial-match redirect URI registrations are not allowed

steps.description: Review token storage practices and lifecycle management.

outputs.name: token-storage-findings
outputs.desc: Findings on how tokens are stored in each client type

outputs.name: lifecycle-findings
outputs.desc: Findings on token expiration, rotation, and revocation

process: Check where access tokens are stored (memory, localStorage, cookies, keychain) per client type
Verify that refresh tokens use rotation (each use issues a new refresh token)
Test token revocation: does revoking a token immediately prevent its use
Check access token lifetimes: shorter is better, with refresh token renewal

steps.description: Test for scope escalation by requesting or manipulating token scopes.

outputs.name: scope-escalation-results
outputs.desc: Results of scope escalation tests

outputs.name: consent-bypass-findings
outputs.desc: Any methods to bypass consent for additional scopes

process: Request tokens with scopes beyond what the client is registered for
Test whether token exchange endpoints allow scope escalation
Check whether consent can be bypassed by replaying or modifying authorization responses
Verify that the resource server validates scopes on each API call, not just at token issuance

steps.description: Verify PKCE implementation for public clients.

inputs.name: client-classification
inputs.desc: Classification of clients as public or confidential

outputs.name: pkce-verification-results
outputs.desc: Results of PKCE verification for each public client

outputs.name: authorization-code-interception-risk
outputs.desc: Risk of authorization code interception for clients without PKCE

process: Verify that all public clients use PKCE (code_challenge and code_verifier)
Test whether the authorization server accepts authorization code exchange without PKCE for public clients
Verify that S256 (SHA-256) is required, not plain code challenge method
Check that code_verifier length meets minimum requirements (43 characters)

steps.description: Scan for token leakage in logs, referrer headers, browser history, and error messages.

outputs.name: token-leakage-findings
outputs.desc: All instances of token leakage found

outputs.name: oauth-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete OAuth implementation security report

process: Check server logs for tokens in query parameters, headers, or request bodies that are logged
Test whether tokens appear in browser history via URL fragments or query parameters
Check referrer headers: do pages with tokens in the URL leak them to third parties
Compile all OAuth findings into the security report with severity ratings and remediation

description: Assess endpoint security posture by testing patch levels, EDR coverage, disk encryption, application controls, peripheral policies, and firmware integrity.

steps.description: Check OS patch levels and hardening baselines across endpoints.

inputs.name: endpoint-inventory
inputs.desc: Inventory of endpoints to assess (workstations, servers, mobile)

inputs.name: hardening-baselines
inputs.desc: Expected hardening baselines (CIS, STIG, or custom)

outputs.name: patch-status-report
outputs.desc: Patch compliance status for each endpoint

outputs.name: hardening-deviations
outputs.desc: Deviations from the hardening baseline per endpoint

process: Scan endpoints for OS and application patch levels
Compare against the current patch baseline and identify missing critical and high patches
Audit hardening settings against the baseline (local policies, services, open ports)
Flag endpoints with critical deviations that increase attack surface

steps.description: Test endpoint detection and response (EDR) deployment and detection effectiveness.

outputs.name: edr-coverage-results
outputs.desc: EDR deployment coverage and detection test results

outputs.name: edr-gaps
outputs.desc: Endpoints without EDR or with misconfigured EDR

process: Verify EDR agent deployment: which endpoints have it installed, running, and reporting
Test detection by executing known-bad indicators (safe test malware, EICAR, atomic red team tests)
Check whether EDR is configured in detect-only or prevent mode
Identify endpoints where EDR is absent, disabled, or running an outdated version

steps.description: Verify full disk encryption deployment and key management across endpoints.

outputs.name: encryption-status
outputs.desc: Disk encryption status for each endpoint

outputs.name: key-escrow-status
outputs.desc: Recovery key escrow verification results

process: Check each endpoint for full disk encryption (BitLocker, FileVault, LUKS)
Verify that encryption is active (not suspended or partially encrypted)
Confirm recovery keys are escrowed to the management system
Test whether cold boot or DMA attacks could bypass encryption on sample devices

steps.description: Test application whitelisting and execution control policies.

outputs.name: app-control-results
outputs.desc: Results of application control bypass testing

outputs.name: execution-policy-gaps
outputs.desc: Gaps in execution control that allow unauthorized software

process: Test whether unsigned or unapproved executables can run
Attempt bypass techniques: DLL sideloading, script interpreters, LOLBins (living off the land)
Check PowerShell and script execution policies and constrained language mode
Test whether macro execution is controlled in Office applications

steps.description: Test USB and peripheral device control policies.

outputs.name: peripheral-control-results
outputs.desc: Results of peripheral device policy tests

outputs.name: data-exfiltration-risks
outputs.desc: Data exfiltration risks via physical media

process: Test USB mass storage device acceptance on sample endpoints
Test other peripheral types: USB network adapters, USB-to-serial, Bluetooth adapters
Check whether device control policies are enforced by endpoint management or can be bypassed locally
Assess data exfiltration risk if USB storage is permitted

steps.description: Verify secure boot configuration and firmware integrity on endpoints.

outputs.name: firmware-integrity-results
outputs.desc: Secure boot and firmware integrity verification results

outputs.name: endpoint-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete endpoint security assessment report

process: Verify secure boot is enabled and enforcing on each endpoint
Check UEFI firmware version against known vulnerabilities
Verify that firmware update mechanisms are authenticated
Compile all endpoint findings into the final report with severity ratings and remediation priorities

description: Audit a security awareness program by reviewing training content, measuring completion and quiz scores, analyzing phishing simulation trends, and assessing reporting culture.

steps.description: Review security awareness training content for relevance, accuracy, and completeness.

inputs.name: training-materials
inputs.desc: Current security awareness training content and curriculum

inputs.name: threat-landscape
inputs.desc: Current threat landscape relevant to the organization

outputs.name: content-review-findings
outputs.desc: Findings on training content quality, accuracy, and coverage gaps

outputs.name: topic-coverage-matrix
outputs.desc: Matrix showing which security topics are covered and which are missing

process: Review each training module for technical accuracy and up-to-date threat examples
Map training topics against the current threat landscape for the organization
Identify missing topics (MFA fatigue, QR phishing, deepfake voice calls, supply chain attacks)
Assess whether content is engaging or likely to be skipped through

steps.description: Measure training completion rates and quiz scores across the organization.

outputs.name: completion-metrics
outputs.desc: Completion rates by department, role, and seniority

outputs.name: knowledge-retention-gaps
outputs.desc: Topics where quiz scores indicate poor retention

process: Extract completion rates from the training platform by department and role
Analyze quiz scores to identify topics with consistently low scores
Check for completion rate differences between departments (engineering, sales, executives)
Identify repeat non-completers and whether enforcement mechanisms exist

steps.description: Analyze phishing simulation results and click rate trends over time.

inputs.name: training-materials
inputs.desc: Phishing simulation platform data and past campaigns

outputs.name: phishing-trend-analysis
outputs.desc: Click rate trends over time by campaign type and department

outputs.name: high-risk-groups
outputs.desc: Groups with persistently high click rates

process: Compile click rates from all phishing simulation campaigns over the past 12 months
Calculate the trend: are click rates decreasing, stable, or increasing
Break down by campaign difficulty, department, and employee tenure
Identify groups that consistently click at high rates despite repeated training

steps.description: Assess whether employees actively report security concerns and suspicious activity.

outputs.name: reporting-culture-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of security reporting behavior across the organization

outputs.name: report-rate-vs-click-rate
outputs.desc: Comparison of phishing report rates against click rates

process: Calculate the phishing report rate: what percentage of simulated phishing emails are reported
Compare report rates against click rates (reporting should exceed clicking)
Review non-phishing security incident reports submitted by employees
Assess whether there are barriers to reporting (complex process, fear of blame, no feedback)

steps.description: Check whether role-specific security training exists for high-risk roles.

outputs.name: role-training-findings
outputs.desc: Findings on role-specific training coverage

outputs.name: missing-role-training
outputs.desc: Roles that need specialized training but lack it

process: Check for developer-specific training (secure coding, dependency management, secrets handling)
Check for administrator-specific training (privilege management, MFA enforcement, audit logging)
Check for executive-specific training (business email compromise, whale phishing, authority manipulation)
Identify roles with specialized access that have no tailored training program

steps.description: Compile the security awareness audit report with metrics, trends, and improvement recommendations.

outputs.name: awareness-audit-report
outputs.desc: Complete security awareness program audit report

outputs.name: program-improvement-plan
outputs.desc: Prioritized plan for improving the awareness program

process: Consolidate all findings: content gaps, completion gaps, phishing trends, reporting culture, role training
Rate the overall program maturity (initial, developing, established, optimized)
Write specific improvement recommendations prioritized by impact
Produce the final report with executive summary, metrics dashboard, and improvement roadmap
